topics.cli:
Usage: prose [GLOBAL OPTIONS] cli <COMMAND> [ARGUMENTS] [OPTIONS]

OpenProse service and account commands. They reach the hosted OpenProse service
and never prompt. New here? `prose cli service guide` walks through a first
program, a daily schedule, scripting and costs. Commands for this machine
(doctor, config) are listed by `prose --help`.

Commands:
  run                         Run a program on the hosted service, then follow, read or cancel it: submit, watch, show, list, cancel, download, input, quote, share.
  program                     Save your programs and manage their revisions: save, list, show, delete, draft, revisions, visibility.
  example                     Working example programs to read and copy: list, show.
  job                         Run a saved program on a schedule or from a webhook: create, list, show, delete, configure, contract, deliveries, rotate-secret, update.
  wallet                      Balance, usage and credit: balance, usage, events, topup, redeem.
  auth                        Sign in, check or remove the stored key: login, status, logout.
  model                       Hosted models: list.
  result                      Published results of public programs (OWNER/SLUG); a run's own output is `cli run show` or `cli run download`: show, list, publish, unpublish.
  org                         Organizations, members and invitations: list, show, create, default, invitation, invite, member, rename.
  repo                        Repositories the service can read: list.
  package                     Registry packages (no source execution): fetch, list, publish, withdraw.
  service                     Service status, triage, the guide and the command list: triage, status, guide, capabilities, operations.

Examples:
  prose cli run submit hello.prose.md --preview
  prose cli program save hello hello.prose.md --preview
  prose cli example list --json
  prose cli job create --spec-file job.json --preview
  prose cli wallet balance --json
  prose cli auth login
  prose cli model list --json
  prose cli result show exowner1/hello --latest
  prose cli org list --json
  prose cli repo list --json
  prose cli package publish my-package --organization acme --name tool --version 1.0.0 --json
  prose cli service triage --json

Global options:
  --output human|json|jsonl   Output mode; the same as the PROSE_OUTPUT setting.

Run `prose cli <COMMAND> --help` for details. `prose cli service operations --json` prints every command as JSON.
topics.cli auth:
Usage: prose [GLOBAL OPTIONS] cli auth <COMMAND> [ARGUMENTS] [OPTIONS]

Account credentials for the OpenProse service. Every other service command
reads the key these commands manage, or OPENPROSE_API_KEY.

Commands:
  login                       Sign in with the GitHub device flow and store the key in the OS credential store.
  status                      Report whether a credential is available and valid.
  logout                      Remove the stored credential.

Examples:
  prose cli auth login
  prose cli auth status --json
  prose cli auth logout --json

Global options:
  --output human|json|jsonl   Output mode; the same as the PROSE_OUTPUT setting.

Credentials:
  OPENPROSE_API_KEY           API key; a non-empty value wins over the stored key.

Device flow: `cli auth login` prints a one-time code and https://github.com/login/device
on stderr, never the key, and never opens a browser. A person approves the code
there within 15 minutes. An agent without a person sets the variable instead.

Run `prose cli auth <COMMAND> --help` for details. `prose cli service operations --json` prints every command as JSON.

topics.cli job configure:
Usage: prose [GLOBAL OPTIONS] cli job configure <JOB_ID> [OPTIONS]

Replace a schedule job's cadence and run configuration. Schedule jobs only.
Quick form: `cli job configure JOB_ID --interval-seconds N` reads the job and resends its current configuration_revision, revision_token and bindings with the new interval.
Full form: --config-file with the body {"interval_seconds":N,"configuration_revision":R,"revision_token":"T","bindings":[{"program_ref":"OWNER/SLUG@REV","run_configuration":{...}}]}.
Read the current values with `cli job show JOB_ID --json`: status.configuration_revision, status.revision_token (an opaque token), and each status.contracts[] program_ref and run_configuration, under the same names.
run_configuration takes model, environment, reasoning_effort, inputs, files, context_repositories and output as show prints them, except input_entries: move each {name, value} entry into inputs, because every input left out is deleted.
A stale revision_token is SERVICE_WRITE_CONFLICT; while a run of the schedule is in progress the service answers SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (retry later).

Arguments:
  JOB_ID                      Job id.

Options:
  --config-file FILE          Schedule configuration: a JSON object of at most 64 KiB (see above), or -. Give exactly one of --config-file and --interval-seconds.
  --interval-seconds N        New interval (60 to 2678400); the current configuration is read and resent unchanged otherwise.
  --yes                       Confirm this operation; required because it replaces the schedule's cadence and run configuration; the next scheduled run uses them.
  --preview                   Print the planned request of a mutation and send nothing.
  --json                      Print one JSON result; the same as the global --output json.
  --help                      Show help for this command.

Examples:
  prose cli job configure 3c1a9e57-0b4d-4f2a-9e61-5d7b2c8a4f10 --interval-seconds 3600 --yes

Output: openprose.service-operation/1 (--json).
Exit codes: 0 success; 2 invalid invocation, configuration or CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED; 10 service or credential error; 24 interrupted.

topics.cli job create:
Usage: prose [GLOBAL OPTIONS] cli job create [OPTIONS]

Create a job from a JSON spec. A job starts paid runs on its own, on a schedule or from webhook events, until it is deleted.
Spec keys are snake_case. `type` is required; `cli job list` prints every type with its config_fields. Each type accepts the keys listed under this command's `spec` in `cli service operations --json`; every problem is reported at once.
  Schedule: {"type":"schedule","program_ref":"OWNER/SLUG@REV","interval_seconds":86400}
    interval_seconds 60 to 2678400 (86400 is once a day). The first run starts about one second after the job is created, then one every interval.
    Cron expressions and a time of day are not supported.
    Optional: model, reasoning_effort, environment, inputs (name -> string), files, repository_url, repository_branch, output.
  Webhook: {"type":"webhook","name":"NAME","delivery_mode":"test"}
    optional name, program_ref, receiver, receiver_secret, reply, reply_secret; delivery_mode test or live. Without program_ref it starts no runs: no hold, effect write.
REV is the program's program.rev_id (printed by `cli program save` and `cli program show OWNER/SLUG`), not its commit_id.

Options:
  --spec-file FILE            Job spec: a JSON object of at most 64 KiB (see above), or - for standard input. Required.
  --yes                       Confirm this operation; required because the job starts paid runs on its own schedule or events until it is deleted (a webhook with no program starts none until one is attached).
  --preview                   Print the planned request of a mutation and send nothing.
  --json                      Print one JSON result; the same as the global --output json.
  --help                      Show help for this command.

Examples:
  prose cli job create --spec-file job.json --preview
  prose cli job create --spec-file job.json --yes

Output: openprose.service-operation/1 (--json).
Exit codes: 0 success; 2 invalid invocation, configuration or CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED; 10 service or credential error; 24 interrupted.

topics.cli run submit:
Usage: prose [GLOBAL OPTIONS] cli run submit [FILE] [OPTIONS]

Run a program on the hosted service and stream it until it finishes, detaches or the deadline passes.
Inputs: --input KEY=VALUE overrides the same key from --inputs-file.
A --wait shorter than the run exits 21 with details.resumeArgv: the run continues, and that command follows it again. Never submit again to resume; that starts a second paid run.

Arguments:
  FILE                        Program file, or - for standard input. Omit when --from is given.

Options:
  --from [OWNER/]SLUG[@REV]   Run a saved program; a bare SLUG is your own program. @REV is a rev_id, or @N (@revN) for revision N of your own program; without @REV the latest revision is pinned.
  --input KEY=VALUE|KEY=@FILE
                              Program input; @FILE reads UTF-8 text of at most 1 MiB. It overrides the same key from --inputs-file. Repeatable.
  --inputs-file FILE          JSON object of string inputs; an --input of the same key wins.
  --model MODEL               Hosted model id (see `cli model list`). Default: the service's default_model (`cli model list`).
  --reasoning-effort EFFORT   Reasoning effort supported by the model. One of: minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh.
  --environment ENV           Where the run executes (for example builtin: file tools only; linux: a shell without network access). Web access is through the browser:interact tool. Default: the service's default environment.
  --runtime RUNTIME           Runtime offered by the service. Default: the service's default runtime.
  --repo OWNER/NAME[@BRANCH]  Read-only repository context. Repeatable.
  --commit-output OWNER/NAME[@BRANCH]
                              Writable repository that receives the run's commit.
  --detach                    Return as soon as the run id is known.
  --wait DURATION             Stop following after this long and exit 21 (for example 90s, 10m, 2h; maximum 6h). The run continues. Default: 30m.
  --session UUID              Use this session UUID instead of a new one (recovery only).
  --yes                       Confirm this operation; required because it starts a paid run: a hold (money set aside from the wallet, not the price) is reserved now, and the run's price is charged when it settles.
  --preview                   Print the planned request of a mutation and send nothing.
  --json                      Print one JSON result; the same as the global --output json.
  --help                      Show help for this command.

Examples:
  prose cli run submit hello.prose.md --preview
  prose cli run submit hello.prose.md --yes
  prose cli run submit --from exowner1/hello --input topic=rain --yes --detach --json

Output: openprose.service-operation/1 (--json) or openprose.service-event/1 lines (--output jsonl). The run id is result.runId (and result.run.run_id once the run ends); the answer is result.run.response.
Exit codes: 0 success; 2 invalid invocation, configuration or CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED; 10 service or credential error; 21 deadline or detached: the run id is known and the run continues (resume with details.resumeArgv); 22 run failed, or submission ambiguous (recover with details.resumeArgv: the same session with --detach, never a new run); 24 cancelled on the service.

grammar.placement: Global options precede `cli`; operation options follow the command path. A rejected global option is an INVOCATION_INVALID error only in the global position; an operation may define its own option of the same name (for example `cli run submit --model`). An operation option or common flag before `cli` (`prose --json cli run list`) is never forwarded to the language: it is an INVOCATION_INVALID error whose suggestedArgv moves it after the command path. In --json and --output json|jsonl every error of a `cli` command line, including an invocation error for a near miss, a misplaced flag or an invalid global, is the openprose.service-operation/1 envelope with the error as `problem`: `operation` is `cli` when the argv names no operation. A bare openprose.runner-error/1 is only for the language and the runner commands (`cli doctor`, `cli harness`, `cli config`, `cli cleanup`).

CANCELLED.meaning: The runner was cancelled before semantic completion.

CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED.meaning: This service operation requires explicit confirmation.

Create a job from a JSON spec. A job starts paid runs on its own, on a schedule or from webhook events, until it is deleted.
Spec keys are snake_case. `type` is required; `cli job list` prints every type with its config_fields. Each type accepts the keys listed under this command's `spec` in `cli service operations --json`; every problem is reported at once.
  Schedule: {"type":"schedule","program_ref":"OWNER/SLUG@REV","interval_seconds":86400}
    interval_seconds 60 to 2678400 (86400 is once a day). The first run starts about one second after the job is created, then one every interval.
    Cron expressions and a time of day are not supported.
    Optional: model, reasoning_effort, environment, inputs (name -> string), files, repository_url, repository_branch, output.
  Webhook: {"type":"webhook","name":"NAME","delivery_mode":"test"}
    optional name, program_ref, receiver, receiver_secret, reply, reply_secret; delivery_mode test or live. Without program_ref it starts no runs: no hold, effect write.
REV is the program's program.rev_id (printed by `cli program save` and `cli program show OWNER/SLUG`), not its commit_id.

Change a webhook job's settings. The spec is a partial JSON object with any of name, receiver, receiver_secret, delivery_mode (test or live), reply and reply_secret, for example {"name":"NAME"} (website-change jobs take url, interval_seconds and mode). Any other key is refused locally.
Schedules are refused (SERVICE_REQUEST_REJECTED); change them with `cli job configure JOB_ID --interval-seconds N` or `cli job configure JOB_ID --config-file FILE`.

Replace a schedule job's cadence and run configuration. Schedule jobs only.
Quick form: `cli job configure JOB_ID --interval-seconds N` reads the job and resends its current configuration_revision, revision_token and bindings with the new interval.
Full form: --config-file with the body {"interval_seconds":N,"configuration_revision":R,"revision_token":"T","bindings":[{"program_ref":"OWNER/SLUG@REV","run_configuration":{...}}]}.
Read the current values with `cli job show JOB_ID --json`: status.configuration_revision, status.revision_token (an opaque token), and each status.contracts[] program_ref and run_configuration, under the same names.
run_configuration takes model, environment, reasoning_effort, inputs, files, context_repositories and output as show prints them, except input_entries: move each {name, value} entry into inputs, because every input left out is deleted.
A stale revision_token is SERVICE_WRITE_CONFLICT; while a run of the schedule is in progress the service answers SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE (retry later).

views.cli service capabilities:
OpenProse service commands: capabilities. `prose cli service capabilities --json` prints this page as one JSON document.

Usage: prose [--output human|json|jsonl] cli <command> [ARGUMENTS] [OPTIONS]
Global options such as --output go before `cli`; command options go after the command. A mistyped or misplaced word is never guessed: the command exits 2 and its error shows the corrected command to run instead.
Common options: --json, --yes, --preview, --help, --no-color.

Environment variables:
  OPENPROSE_API_KEY           API key; a non-empty value wins over the stored key.
  PROSE_OUTPUT                Output mode (human, json or jsonl) when neither --output nor --json is given.
  XDG_STATE_HOME              Base directory of the local run journal.
  PROSE_DEBUG                 Set to 1 to print a hosted run's error text as the service sent it instead of its mapped message.

Exit codes (0 is success; with --json, the error's code is in problem.code):
  0   success
  2   CONFIG_INVALID                Runner configuration is invalid.
  2   CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED         This service operation requires explicit confirmation.
  2   EXAMPLE_NOT_VIEWABLE          This example is published outside the OpenProse service and cannot be shown here.
  2   INVOCATION_INVALID            Runner invocation is invalid.
  10  CREDENTIAL_STORE_UNAVAILABLE  The operating system credential store is unavailable.
  10  DEVICE_AUTH_EXPIRED           Device authorization expired. Retryable.
  10  DEVICE_AUTH_FAILED            Device authorization failed.
  10  GITHUB_LINK_REQUIRED          This operation needs a linked GitHub account on the OpenProse account.
  10  SERVICE_ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED     The OpenProse account is suspended.
  10  SERVICE_AUTH_REQUIRED         OpenProse service authentication is required.
  10  SERVICE_BALANCE_INSUFFICIENT  The OpenProse wallet balance is insufficient for this operation.
  10  SERVICE_FEATURE_DISABLED      This capability is not available for this account.
  10  SERVICE_PREMIUM_MODEL_LOCKED  This model is a premium model that unlocks with any wallet top-up.
  10  SERVICE_PROTOCOL_INVALID      The OpenProse service returned an invalid response.
  10  SERVICE_REQUEST_REJECTED      The OpenProse service rejected the request.
  10  SERVICE_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND    The requested OpenProse service resource was not found.
  10  SERVICE_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE    The OpenProse service response exceeded the client limit.
  10  SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE           The OpenProse service is unavailable. Retryable.
  10  SERVICE_WRITE_CONFLICT        The OpenProse service reported a conflicting write.
  21  HOSTED_RUN_DETACHED           The client stopped following the hosted run before its outcome arrived; the run was not cancelled.
  21  SERVICE_WATCH_DEADLINE        The watch deadline elapsed before the hosted run finished; the run continues.
  22  HOSTED_RUN_FAILED             The hosted run finished without completing successfully.
  22  RUN_SUBMISSION_AMBIGUOUS      The run submission could not be confirmed and was not repeated.
  24  CANCELLED                     The runner was cancelled before semantic completion. Retryable.
  24  HOSTED_RUN_CANCELLED          The hosted run was cancelled on the service and will not continue.
  70  INTERNAL_ERROR                The runner encountered an internal fault.
